papers.title: The Head Complexity of Boolean Functions in Single-Layer Attention

summary.tldr: A study on single-layer attention-only models establishes that $k$ heads are necessary and sufficient to compute $k$-bit parity, regardless of embedding dimension or numerical precision.
key_points: Unconditional lower bounds show $k$ attention heads can compute $k$-bit parity but cannot compute $(k+1)$-bit parity, even with unbounded precision and embedding dimension.
The parity lower bound relies on an alternating-sum obstruction where clearing softmax denominators leaves decision polynomial monomials missing at least one input bit.
A compactness theorem proves any function computable by the model can be implemented with embedding dimension and precision bounded by head count, alphabet size, and sequence length.
General $n$-bit binary functions require at most $2^n$ heads (one per monomial in multilinear expansion) and at least $\Omega(2^n/n^2)$ heads for almost all functions.
The alternating-sum obstruction proof technique extends to establish lower bounds for multi-hop induction-head tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes fundamental computational limits of single-layer transformers, proving that increasing embedding dimension or numerical precision cannot compensate for a lack of attention heads.

papers.title: Two-Stage Reinforcement Learning for Sound and Adversarial Test Generation in Code LLMs

summary.tldr: Test Cases Scaling (TCS) uses a two-stage reinforcement learning framework to auto-generate sound and adversarial test cases based on a code solver's evolving failure modes.
key_points: TCS trains a test generator from a rolling policy-aligned buffer using a two-stage reinforcement learning approach.
Stage 1 generates test cases that are consistent with the reference solution to ensure soundness.
Stage 2 restricts the buffer to current failure modes to learn discriminative counterexample tests.
The framework improves pass@1 performance and inference-time answer selection on the TACO and LiveCodeBench benchmarks.
The resulting test generator can effectively select correct solutions among outputs produced by other LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: TCS automates the creation of high-quality, discriminative test cases, improving code LLM evaluation, output selection, and overall model accuracy without relying on scarce human-written tests.

papers.title: Extracting Forgotten Prompts from Targeted Unlearned Models

summary.tldr: Targeted Active Search (TAS) extracts forgotten prompts from unlearned LLMs using retained data and black-box access under a limited query budget.
key_points: Identifies forgotten entities by querying the model with canonical templates and an entity pool using black-box access.
Instantiates prompt templates with identified entities to reconstruct exact forgotten prompts.
Achieves 100% accuracy in identifying forgotten entities and reconstructs up to 95% of forgotten prompts across three unlearning methods (NPO, DPO, LUNAR), three datasets, and three LLMs.
Reduces required model queries by up to 99.7% compared to naive probing techniques.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that refusal-aligned machine unlearning methods fail to keep the target forgotten prompts private from black-box adversaries.

papers.title: Doesn't Stop Reasoning: Analysis of Spurious CoT Termination

summary.tldr: Injecting an end-of-think token to early-exit reasoning in LRMs causes spurious CoT termination, where reasoning continues into the answering phase unless attention to the injected token is artificially boosted.
key_points: Training-free early-exit methods use an injected end-of-think (EoT) token to force LRMs from the reasoning phase into the answering phase.
Injecting an EoT token often fails to cause a clean transition; models exhibit spurious CoT termination where reasoning behavior continues in the answering phase until a second EoT is regenerated.
The length of the spurious reasoning span in the answering phase scales proportionally with the number of reasoning tokens saved by the early exit.

The authors introduce Exit-token Attention Biasing (EAB) to increase attention to the injected EoT, which reduces spurious CoT termination and answering-phase length across four LRMs and five benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Matching an LRM's explicit think-block format via token injection is insufficient to control its internal state, requiring attention manipulation to reliably force early exits.

papers.title: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments

summary.tldr: Terminal-Universe is a framework that reconstructs scalable, executable code environments from terminal agent trajectories by replaying file operations and generating missing dependencies.
key_points: Reconstructs workspace environments from tool-execution histories by restoring files to pre-modification states and using a completion agent to infer missing files.
Scales task breadth via cross-workspace queries across dependent codebases and depth via multi-round interactive sessions using a user agent.
Generated 37.3k task-sufficient environments from public terminal agent trajectories.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-27B on the dataset improved single-round Terminal-Bench 2.1 performance by 11.9 points and multi-round EvoCode-Bench v2 MT@4 by 13.8 points.
summary.why_it_matters: It converts static, single-use agent trajectories into reusable, verifiable training environments and complex multi-turn tasks at scale.

papers.title: Environment Evolution for Terminal Agents

summary.tldr: Environment evolution improves terminal agent training by incrementally increasing environment difficulty off-policy and scheduling these evolved environments generation by generation.
key_points: Addresses the limitation of on-policy co-evolution methods, which fail to provide continuous learning signals as frontier models become stronger.
Derives three specific evolution directions that impact environment difficulty directly from the multi-turn learning objective.
Implements difficulty progression off-policy using a loop-engineered multi-agent harness.
Validated with quantitative rollouts on Hy4 preview, Claude Opus 5, and GPT-5.6 Sol to confirm generated environment difficulty.
Yielded performance improvements of 14.4 and 18.0 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1 when applied to long-horizon RL training of Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.
summary.why_it_matters: Off-policy environment evolution provides a scalable framework to continuously challenge and improve strong terminal agents as frontier models outgrow static or on-policy benchmarks.

papers.title: Representational alignment yields generalizable safety in language models

summary.tldr: Researchers developed representational similarity optimization, a method that aligns LLM latent representations with human moral prototype structures to improve adversarial robustness without supervising text output.
key_points: Evaluations across 23 LLMs revealed that standard models fail to cleanly separate opposing moral categories or preserve fine-grained typicality, regardless of parameter size or alignment stage.
Using 251,334 moral annotations, standard behavioral alignment learned response-level moral judgments but left internal categorization unchanged, increasing adversarial vulnerability.

Representational similarity optimization directly reshaped latent space categorization, resulting in modest gains in explicit judgments but consistent improvements in adversarial robustness across model scales, benchmarks, and attack strategies.
summary.why_it_matters: Aligning internal model representations rather than surface-level output responses offers a novel strategy to create language models that generalize safety across diverse adversarial attacks.

papers.title: Interface-Induced Trajectory Censoring

summary.tldr: Interface-induced trajectory censoring causes serving stacks to silently drop valid agent tool-calls, creating artificial performance collapses that depend entirely on interaction mismatches between chat templates and output parsers.
key_points: On BFCL v4, switching only the serving adapter changed model scores from 0.00 to 0.96/0.19, with a 2x2 ANOVA revealing all variation sits in the template-parser interaction term.
Across Qwen2.5-Coder sizes up to 32B on tau-bench, server-parsed calls remained at 0/100 while actual emitted well-formed calls reached 80/100 (72 calibrated).
In verl's RL training loop (AgentLoop) at 7B, 45 of 115 generations contained complete tool calls, but 0 were parsed or executed by the interface.
Adding a strict:true flag eliminated Llama-3.1-8B's 23% rate of hallucinating the task function itself as a callable tool.
Fixing the adapter at evaluation time increased parsed calls from 0 to 84 and rescued tasks from 0 to 9, though the pass rate change (53 to 62) was not statistically significant.
summary.why_it_matters: Reported tool-call metrics reflect the model-interface stack rather than pure model capabilities, risking flawed evaluations and silent failures during reinforcement learning training.

papers.title: RATL: Learning from Retrieved Residuals for Robust Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

summary.tldr: RATL is a plug-in forecasting framework that retrieves historical residual errors from a frozen base model to perform learned feedback correction at inference time.
key_points: Shifts the retrieval target from raw historical values to model-specific historical forecast residuals stored in a train-only memory.
Employs a set-aware router over forecast blocks and variables to select and combine retrieved residual trajectories while respecting causal constraints.
Uses validation-based correction-strength selection to prevent over-injecting residual feedback.
Evaluated primarily on iTransformer, demonstrating performance improvements as a plug-in module across multiple forecasting backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables existing time-series models to leverage past forecast errors dynamically at inference without retraining the underlying base architecture.

papers.title: GraFT: A Training-Free Framework for Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models via 3D Scene Graphs

summary.tldr: GraFT is a training-free framework that enhances multimodal LLM 3D spatial reasoning by extracting geometry, allocentric BEV renderings, and egocentric visual attributes from a 3D scene graph.
key_points: Eliminates the need for task-specific fine-tuning or dedicated 3D geometry encoders by using a compact 3D scene graph (3DSG).
Provides deterministic geometric measurements via symbolic tools operating on the 3DSG.
Generates bird's-eye-view (BEV) renderings for allocentric layout understanding and task-relevant egocentric frames for visual-attribute grounding.
Improves CIDEr by 27% on ScanQA over the same-backbone baseline and boosts frozen MLLM performance by up to 65% on VSI-Bench.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables frozen, general-purpose MLLMs to perform complex 3D spatial reasoning without expensive training data or model architecture modifications.

papers.title: Xiaomi-TabLDM: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report

summary.tldr: Xiaomi-TabLDM is a tabular foundation model pretrained exclusively on synthetic data from structural causal models, achieving top-tier regression and classification performance via in-context learning without task-specific fine-tuning.
key_points: Pretrained entirely on expanded synthetic tabular data generated using structural causal models (SCMs).
Employs a three-stage training strategy incorporating dual-stream feature grouping, lightweight Attention Residual, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Ranks 1st on OpenML-CTR23 and 2nd on regression across TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO benchmarks.
Reduces computational overhead on TabArena regression compared to top-ranked TabFM, using 82% less training time and 68% less prediction time.
Supports test-time compute scaling, allowing inference-time computational allocation to consistently increase predictive accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that synthetic pretraining via causal models can yield competitive tabular foundation models that significantly reduce inference latency and training overhead.

papers.title: Conditioning Degenerate Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: A new framework uses causal optimal transport to establish approximate loss functions and minimum-entropy guidance for degenerate diffusion processes with singular coefficients and non-smooth densities.
key_points: Addresses conditioned generative models where diffusion processes have singular coefficients and underlying densities are non-smooth or nonexistent.
Formulates guidance as a minimum-entropy control problem using causal optimal transport.
Leverages the predictable representation property of conditioned diffusion processes via well-posed martingale problems in the style of Üstünel.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables principled guidance for conditional diffusion models in degenerate settings where standard score-based methods fail due to non-smooth or singular densities.

papers.title: Beyond Endpoint Scores: Time- and Capacity-Conditioned Evaluation of Continual Knowledge Updating

summary.tldr: A study on continual knowledge updating demonstrates that method rankings reverse based on evaluation timing, replay LoRA rank, and query formulations, proving single-checkpoint evaluations insufficient.
key_points: Evaluated a periodic hierarchy against cumulative replay across a 24-month Wikidata stream using Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.2-1B models.
On Qwen2.5-1.5B, the periodic hierarchy's 5.0-point advantage over rank-8 replay flipped into an 11.6-point deficit when compared against rank-72 replay.
At high ranks, consolidation-aligned endpoints indicated a tie, whereas time-averaged evaluation showed replay leading by 9 to 13 points.
Proposes an evaluation protocol requiring time-series trajectories, capacity sweeps, and retention-stability-cost frontiers rather than single-checkpoint scalar rankings.
Reclassifies the periodic hierarchy method as a lower-update-cost operating point rather than an absolute quality winner.
summary.why_it_matters: Assessing continual learning techniques solely at a single final checkpoint or fixed adapter rank risks misidentifying superior methods, requiring multi-dimensional capacity and time sweeps for valid benchmarking.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Learning Dynamics of Attention-Indexed Models

summary.tldr: Researchers analyzed the high-dimensional learning dynamics of attention-indexed models, demonstrating how different attention parameterizations create implicit architectural biases that dictate optimization speed and sample complexity.
key_points: In the high-dimensional limit, the population-loss landscape is defined by finite trace order parameters, whereas online SGD is governed by an infinite matrix-moment hierarchy that can be truncated with exponential precision.
Direct optimization of a full attention matrix S in R^{d x d} can trap online SGD in uninformative states.
Tied attention (S = W W^T) induces automatic symmetry breaking, enabling weak recovery in Theta(d^2 log d) samples.

Untied attention (S = U V^T) exhibits a fast-slow timescale separation where pre-activation means evolve fast and overlaps evolve slowly; weak recovery requires the fast dynamics to break initial symmetry.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how attention matrix parameterization acts as an implicit bias provides a theoretical foundation for designing faster-converging and more sample-efficient transformer architectures.

papers.title: Last Translation Benchmark

summary.tldr: The Last Translation Benchmark (LTBv1) is a live, multimodal, human-authored dataset designed to break state-of-the-art machine translation models using handcrafted, rule-based verification for actionable evaluation.
key_points: LTBv1 includes peer-reviewed texts, images, audio, and videos specifically crafted to expose failure cases in leading machine translation models.
Initial dataset version LTBv1 consists of human-authored contributions accepted prior to September 1st, 2026, with plans for continuous, live updates.
Replaces standard automated metrics and subjective human evaluation with handcrafted, example-specific verification rules to ensure actionable, objective, and reproducible error detection.
summary.why_it_matters: By providing adversarial, rule-verified test cases, LTB prevents metric saturation and reward-hacking, offering a reliable methodology to measure translation progress and pinpoint specific model weaknesses.

papers.title: Alignment-Free Text-Audiobox for Voice Dubbing and Full-Duplex Dialogue Synthesis

summary.tldr: Text-Audiobox is an alignment-free 3B-parameter Diffusion Transformer using DAC-VAE latents to perform voice dubbing and full-duplex dialogue synthesis directly from raw text.
key_points: Uses a latent diffusion framework with DAC-VAE features that compress 48 kHz waveforms into a 25 Hz sequence, yielding over 10x higher compression than EnCodec.
Eliminates forced alignment and explicit duration prediction by using cross-attention over raw text embeddings from an off-the-shelf text encoder.
Pretrained a 3B-parameter model on 480k hours of monolingual speech, followed by SFT for cross-lingual dubbing and emotional full-duplex dialogue.
Supports up to ~1 minute single-shot generation and long-form audio via a multi-diffusion scheme with a multi-stage automated metric reranking strategy.
summary.why_it_matters: It removes the need for explicit duration modeling and phone alignment tools in voice dubbing while enabling native, highly expressive full-duplex conversational AI.

papers.title: RuleMem: Active Rule Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents

summary.tldr: RuleMem is an active memory framework that induces natural-language Horn clauses from long-term dialogue histories to actively guide evidence retrieval and reasoning in conversational agents.
key_points: Constructs natural-language Horn clauses from past interactions to represent reusable logical rules rather than passive facts.
Validates induced rules using a Rule Perplexity Consistency (RPC) mechanism.
Utilizes induced rules to retrieve semantically distant evidence and supply an explicit logical structure for answer generation.
Outperformed 14 baselines on the LoCoMo benchmark, exceeding the baseline average accuracy by 27.47 points (a 54.3% relative improvement), and evaluated on LongMemEval_s*.
summary.why_it_matters: It bridges semantic gaps in long-term conversational QA by replacing passive fact retrieval with active, rule-based logical reasoning over temporally dispersed dialogue history.

papers.title: Select, Compress, Reinvest: A Controlled Study of Visual-Token Allocation in Long-Video MLLMs

summary.tldr: A controlled study isolates visual-token allocation variables in long-video MLLMs, showing that query-based frame selection and reinvesting spatial compression savings yield significant performance gains.
key_points: Selecting eight query-relevant frames beats sixteen uniformly sampled frames by 6.9 points on LongVideoBench's hour-long subset.
Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) matches or comes within 1.0 point of purpose-built frame selectors across all three evaluated benchmarks.
Spatial compression is nearly lossless, costing at most 0.44 points when halving a frame's spatial token budget at fixed timestamps.
Reinvesting compressed token savings to sample twice as many frames at equivalent compute costs increases accuracy by 2 to 3 points.
Evaluating identical selection rules across different harnesses caused performance variance ranging from 0.07 to 3.74 points.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that long-video MLLM performance can be significantly improved without retraining by optimizing frame selection and reinvesting spatial token savings into higher temporal sampling.

papers.title: Rent-a-RAG: Embedding-Space Watermarks for Auditing Third-Party RAG

summary.tldr: DirBucket introduces a provider-side semantic watermarking framework that embeds secret directional biases into document embeddings via paraphrasing to audit unauthorized third-party RAG document reuse from black-box LLM answers.
key_points: DirBucket uses meaning-preserving paraphrases to shift document embeddings toward secret provider-bucket directions.
The framework operates under a black-box model, detecting document reuse despite generator-side paraphrases and multi-provider evidence synthesis.
Experimental evaluation detected non-compliance within 23 audited answers with no non-target activations.
Detection remained effective against adversarial post-answer laundering and transferred to real clinical, cyber-threat-intelligence, and legal corpora without modifications.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a robust, statistically verifiable method for data owners to audit and enforce licensing compliance on non-cooperative third-party RAG platforms.

papers.title: A Circuit for Plural Reference: How LLMs Represent and Retrieve Singular and Plural Entities

summary.tldr: Researchers used mechanistic interpretability and causal interventions to identify the specific attention head circuit LLMs use to represent, identify, and retrieve singular and plural entities for coreference resolution.
key_points: Identified functional attention heads responsible for encoding coreference information, detecting plural references, and transferring data to antecedent selection components.
Used a combination of mechanistic interpretability, attention pattern analysis, and causal intervention techniques to map pronoun prediction circuits.
Found LLMs mirror human preferences by favoring plural pronouns when entities are ontologically similar and joined by the conjunction 'and'.
summary.why_it_matters: Mapping the specific attention circuits for plural reference aids in understanding and improving complex contextual reasoning and coreference resolution in large language models.

papers.title: Remember and Reweight: Enhancing Multi-Agent Debate with Experience Memory and Confidence Estimation

summary.tldr: R^2-MAD enhances multi-agent debate by utilizing historical debate experience memory to correct shared misconceptions through dynamic state-aware retrieval and confidence-weighted peer influence.
key_points: Addresses shared misconception in multi-agent debate, where majority errors are amplified during iterative discussion.
Uses a debate-state-aware retrieval policy to dynamically fetch relevant historical evidence based on current agent consensus levels.
Calculates confidence weights from retrieved experience memory to evaluate per-agent reliability and modulate peer influence.
Outperforms standard single-agent LLMs and existing multi-agent debate baselines across multiple reasoning benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents multi-agent LLM systems from cascading into consensus on incorrect answers by injecting calibrated historical memory and reliability weighting.

papers.title: Lost in Reordering: Structural Sensitivity of Multilingual LLMs under Semantics-Preserving Perturbations

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the IndicReStruct benchmark to reveal that state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs suffer significant reasoning degradation when subjected to semantics-preserving syntactic perturbations in Hindi and Malayalam.
key_points: Evaluated six SOTA LLMs across multiple prompting strategies on two IndicReStruct dataset variants: GSM8K-Reordered (constrained constituent reordering) and GSM8K-Voice (active-passive voice transformation).
Qualitative error analysis demonstrates that mathematical reasoning failures under structural perturbations stem from disruptions in entity-quantity alignment.
Mechanistic interpretability via residual-stream activation patching reveals that intermediate transformer layers contribute most strongly to restoring correct reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings highlight that multilingual LLMs lack robust compositional invariance, making them fragile to surface syntactic variations in free word-order languages despite semantic equivalence.

papers.title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning

summary.tldr: The Seeing Before Synthesizing (SBS) framework improves weakly-supervised dense video captioning by using VLMs to generate visually grounded narratives for inter-event gaps, adaptively detecting transitions from semantic variations.
key_points: Replaces rigid, ungrounded LLM-synthesized transition captions with VLM-generated frame-level narratives across inter-event gaps.
Detects video transition events by measuring semantic variations across the frame-level narratives.
Refines inter-event temporal masks by combining temporal midpoints with semantic change points and tuning mask width to maximize vision-language alignment.
Achieves state-of-the-art results in localization and captioning on the ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a more accurate, visually grounded method for localizing and describing complex, multi-event untrimmed videos without requiring fine-grained event timestamp annotations.

papers.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Human-AI Interaction

summary.tldr: TAHI enables agent test-time adaptation using human-agent interaction data to update context, weights, and an evolving user-specific rubric module.
key_points: Integrates cross-session interaction data into context and model weights while updating an evolving rubric module to capture tacit user criteria.
Evaluated across 30 individuals completing 600 total tasks in writing and visual creation domains.
Improves solo task success by 4.5% to 20.9% within tens of tasks per user.
Evolving rubric module detects 16.0% to 22.3% more failures than rubrics created by LMs or humans alone.
Personalized agents demonstrate cross-user generalization, delivering success improvements of up to 8.8% on other users.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that logging and learning from routine human-agent interactions allows AI agents to rapidly align with personalized, hard-to-specify user criteria while improving general task performance.

papers.title: CORE: Improving Compositional Reasoning in MLLM Embedding via Reranker Distillation

summary.tldr: CORE introduces a Rank-KL objective to distill fine-grained compositional judgments from a multimodal cross-attentive reranker into a dense MLLM embedding model.
key_points: Synthesizes candidate retrieval lists spanning five compositional matching levels to capture subtle attribute-object binding differences.
Uses a listwise Rank-KL distillation objective that forces the embedding model to mimic the reranker's multi-level probability distribution and ranking order.
Evaluations show listwise Rank-KL and pairwise CoSENT utilize multi-level supervision better than standard contrastive learning.
CORE-EMBED-8B achieves a top total average score of 0.666 among embedding models across COLA, SUGARCREPE++, and NEGBENCH benchmarks.
CORE-RERANKER-8B reaches an 82.7% total average (outperforming Jina-Reranker by 10.7 points) and generalizes to MCMR without degrading COCO or Flickr30K performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables dense embedding models to resolve complex compositional logic and attribute bindings without resorting to computationally expensive cross-attention at retrieval time.

security.title: Retrosynthesis of Synthetic Media for Explainable AI Provenance Forensics

summary.tldr: A self-referential retrosynthesis framework enables explainable synthetic media provenance verification under a fixed-generator setting without modifying generator architectures, parameters, or embedding watermarks.
key_points: Uses a jointly optimized encoder-decoder pair to implement a self-embedding mechanism for round-trip consistency verification.
Client inputs are encoded prior to generation, producing outputs that maintain visual fidelity comparable to standard generator outputs.
Decoded images allow resynthesized outputs to be compared against query images to verify if they originated from the target model.
Eliminates the need for architectural modifications, parameter tuning, or explicit watermark embedding.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows platform providers to reliably trace and audit synthetic media origins on MLaaS platforms without sacrificing image quality or altering deployed generative models.

security.title: WeaveMark: Robust and Scalable Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Coded Payload Spreading

summary.tldr: WeaveMark introduces a robust multi-bit LLM watermarking scheme using multi-bit-per-token coded payload spreading, soft-decision error-correcting codes, and unbiased multilayer reweighting to boost capacity and extraction accuracy without degrading text quality.
key_points: Employs multi-bit-per-token payload spreading and soft-decision error-correcting codes to increase capacity and extraction accuracy.
Uses unbiased multilayer reweighting to preserve generation quality and dedicated zero-bit layers to detect watermark presence.
Achieves an 89.8% match rate for 32-bit messages at 200 tokens compared to 20.8% for BiMark.
Sustains an 86.0% match rate under 10% substitution attacks on 16-bit messages at 200 tokens, compared to 30.7% for BiMark.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly improves the reliability of user-identifiable tracking in AI-generated text under editing attacks while preserving output quality.

security.title: Learning-Based Reconstruction Attacks on Coordinate-Obfuscated Point Clouds

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated machine learning-based reconstruction attacks on selective coordinate encryption for point clouds, demonstrating that PointNet and Random Forest models can accurately reconstruct coordinates under sparse encryption schemes.
key_points: Evaluated the security of selective coordinate encryption for point clouds using PointNet and Random Forest reconstruction models.
Tested two specific encryption granularities: X (where all X coordinates are encrypted) and 2X (where every second X coordinate is encrypted).

Found that fully encrypting all X coordinates resists machine learning reconstruction, whereas the 2X scheme leaks enough spatial and geometric correlation from unencrypted neighbors to allow accurate recovery.
Demonstrated that the security of partial coordinate encryption depends heavily on the specific encryption granularity employed.
summary.why_it_matters: Lightweight selective encryption schemes for volumetric video must carefully select coordinate granularity to prevent adversaries from recovering protected visual content via spatial machine learning models.

summary.tldr: A new poisoning attack, PGM-attack, inserts adversarial keys into PGM-indexes to inflate segment counts and index size by up to 120x.
key_points: PGM-attack sequentially inserts adversarial keys to exploit vulnerabilities in optimal piecewise linear approximations (PLAs).
Poisoning 10% of dataset keys increases PGM-index segment count and overall memory size by up to 120x.
The authors derived an instance-dependent theoretical upper bound, certifying PGM-attack achieves at least 52% of the optimal worst-case segment inflation (within 1.92x of the bound).
The attack successfully transfers to other learned indexes, particularly those relying on PLA construction methods.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that optimal PLA-based learned indexes are inherently vulnerable to space-inflation attacks highlights the need for robustness-aware optimization objectives in data structure design.

security.title: Agentic Settlement Protocol: An Application Profile for Refundable, Delayed-Fulfilment Agent Commerce on Stablecoin Rails

summary.tldr: The Agentic Settlement Protocol (ASP) defines an application profile over on-chain authorize-and-capture escrow on the XDC Network for delayed-fulfilment, refundable autonomous agent commerce.
key_points: Uses a three-deadline hold model separating issuance deadline, escrow expiry, and inventory expiry by a submission-inclusion-finality margin to prevent issuing inventory against reclaimable funds.
Features a fulfilment-verification ladder that specifies trusted capture triggers, attestation proofs, and associated challenge windows.
Enforces engine-authoritative partial refunds with strict refund-liquidity ordering, atomic exposure reservation, per-seller credit limits, and a single-currency-per-charge invariant.
Provides a normative interface specification including an x402 scheme, vault ABI, operator/connector APIs, and a self-dealing-resistant distributor revenue share model.
summary.why_it_matters: ASP enables autonomous agents to handle complex, non-atomic commercial transactions like travel bookings and physical orders that require off-chain fulfilment, challenge windows, and cancellations.

summary.tldr: NVIDIA has agreed to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion while maintaining its platform neutrality and multi-hardware support.
key_points: NVIDIA will purchase Hugging Face for $12,930,300,000.
Hugging Face currently hosts over 3 million models, 500,000 datasets, and 1 million applications, serving 18 million users and 200,000 companies.
NVIDIA is the platform's largest contributor, having released over 500 models and 250 open datasets on Hugging Face.
The platform will remain open and vendor-neutral, continuing to support multi-cloud, multi-accelerator deployment without requiring NVIDIA hardware.
summary.why_it_matters: The acquisition combines NVIDIA's infrastructure with Hugging Face's developer ecosystem while explicitly preserving open-weight model availability and non-NVIDIA hardware compatibility.

summary.tldr: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Astra for developers, featuring improved prompt understanding, higher attention to detail, and specialized capabilities in generating 3D models.
key_points: Demonstrates improved prompt comprehension and greater attention to detail across general tasks.
Capable of generating complex, sophisticated outputs, with specific strengths in 3D model creation.
Successfully renders complex 3D scenes including gardens, shipyards, animals, cityscapes, and Dyson spheres.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers gain access to an upgraded model capable of generating significantly more sophisticated outputs and complex 3D renderings.

vendors.title: The Pelican comparison grid for Astra is pretty interesting

summary.tldr: A comparative evaluation of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra against GPT-5.6 models on SVG generation tasks demonstrates significantly improved visual fidelity and lower token consumption despite higher per-token pricing.
key_points: GPT-6 Astra costs $10/M input and $50/M output tokens compared to GPT-5.6 Sol at $5/M input and $30/M output tokens.
Astra generates higher-quality SVGs at its lowest reasoning setting ('low', costing $0.0955) than any GPT-5.6 Sol reasoning level.
Astra and Luna both used 16 input tokens for the prompt, compared to 26 input tokens used by Sol and Terra.
Astra does not support a 'reasoning=none' setting, and levels below 'max' fail to reliably render pelican legs on both sides of the bicycle frame.
summary.why_it_matters: Astra's reduced token usage offsets its higher base pricing, making it more cost-effective than GPT-5.6 for complex generative SVG tasks.
